    - complementary:
      - heading "THEOREM (Rule)" [level=2]
      - paragraph: In a cyclic quadrilateral ABCD,
      - strong: ∠A + ∠C = 180° ∠B + ∠D = 180°
      - separator
      - heading "Converse (Cyclicity Test)" [level=3]
      - paragraph: If either opposite pair sums to 180°, then the quadrilateral is cyclic.
    - article:
      - heading "WHY IT WORKS" [level=2]
      - paragraph: Opposite angles subtend arcs with the other two vertices on them.
      - paragraph: ∠A and ∠C stand on arcs BC and DA that together make the full circle.
      - paragraph: ⌢BC + ⌢DA = 360° ⇒ ∠A + ∠C = ½(360°) = 180°.
      - paragraph: Similarly, ∠B + ∠D = 180°.
    - article:
      - heading "WORKED EXAMPLE" [level=2]
      - paragraph: If ∠A = 112°, find ∠C.
      - text: A B C D
      - paragraph: ∠A + ∠C = 180° 112° + ∠C = 180° ∠C = 180° − 112°
      - strong: ∠C = 68°
    - article:
      - heading "COMMON MISCONCEPTION" [level=2]:
        - img
        - text: COMMON MISCONCEPTION
      - paragraph: Adjacent angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are not generally supplementary.
      - paragraph: Only opposite angles sum to 180°.
      - paragraph: "From the figure: ∠A + ∠B = 112° + 74° = 186°"
      - text: (Not necessarily 180°)
